modules.$comment: The target is computed, never hardcoded. Documents on this machine is both redirected to OneDrive and localised - the real path is OneDrive\Documenten - so %USERPROFILE%\Documents would be wrong here and wrong in a different way on another machine. {psprofiledir} resolves through PowerShell's own $PROFILE, which is correct under redirection, localisation, and neither. profile.ps1 is the AllHosts profile, so it also loads in the VS Code terminal and the ISE. PowerShell 7 reads a sibling Documents\PowerShell directory instead; when pwsh enters the picture, add a second link to it with skipIfParentMissing. Machine-local additions go in Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 beside it, which stays unversioned.

modules.todo: Wire up .vimrc, .ideavimrc, .vsvimrc. Supersedes install-vim-windows.cmd, which uses a bare mklink /H with no conflict checking. Note .vimrc currently has no link on this machine.

BLOCKED on de-tangling the link direction first. On the machine where it was set up, the repo's `nvim` entry is itself a symlink pointing OUT to %LOCALAPPDATA%
vim - the opposite direction from every other entry. Git followed it when adding, so 17 real files are tracked at mode 100644 and a fresh clone does get the actual config; content is not at risk. The gap is that a fresh clone leaves nvim/ as an ordinary directory nobody reads, because nothing links %LOCALAPPDATA%
vim to it. Wiring the obvious link here would be self-referential on the original machine, where repo/nvim already points at that exact target. Fix by inverting it there - replace the repo symlink with the real directory, then link %LOCALAPPDATA%
vim back to it - after which the same link works everywhere and this module can be populated.

modules.$comment: The background image is referenced as the relative path assets/terminal_bg.png. Windows Terminal 1.24+ resolves backgroundImage relative to settings.json, so nothing machine-specific is baked into the shared file and no environment variable is needed. Linking the assets directory in alongside settings.json means it resolves whether WT looks beside the symlink or beside the file the symlink points at. 8wekyb3d8bbwe is Microsoft's publisher hash and is constant for Store apps, so the package path needs no globbing. Only the stable channel is managed: Preview is installed here too but keeps its own settings, and adopting it would mean overwriting a working config - link it deliberately with -Force if you ever want the two channels shared. On a WT older than 1.24 the relative path will not resolve; the fallback is an absolute-free %WT_SETTINGS_DIR%\assets\terminal_bg.png plus an env entry pointing that variable at {repo}\windows-terminal.
